missing_spec_content.spec_text: the changing political and trading relationships with the wider world
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson covers changing trading relationships but not changing political relationships. The only political link is China lending money and building infrastructure: "China has also lent money and built roads and railways, though some worry this leaves Nigeria in debt" (keyPoints[3].content). Nigeria's political links with the wider world are not taught, for example its Commonwealth membership and suspension, and its roles in the African Union, the UN and peacekeeping. keyPoints[0].content mentions British rule and military governments only as internal context, not as changing relationships with other countries.

factual_errors.text: Aid is given, not lent: do not confuse it with loans or investment.
factual_errors.correction: Aid can include loans on easier terms than normal (concessional loans, low or no interest). Much multilateral aid from the World Bank, which the lesson itself uses as its example in keyPoints[3].content, is lent rather than given. Aid should be distinguished from commercial loans and investment, not from all loans.

factual_errors.text: Confusing aid with loans, investment or TNCs. Aid is given.
factual_errors.correction: Aid includes grants and also concessional (low-interest) loans, for example from the World Bank. Calling every loan 'not aid' is wrong. The distinction is between aid and commercial loans or investment.

factual_errors.text: It earns most of its money from selling oil abroad, yet many of its people are still poor.
factual_errors.correction: Oil and gas make up most of Nigeria's export earnings (the lesson's own figure is about 86% of goods exports), but only a small share of its GDP. Most of Nigeria's economic output comes from services and agriculture. The sentence should say oil earns most of its export money, not most of its money.
